root_idea.summary: The root concerns a person's abasement, shame, or disgrace, whether experienced inwardly or imposed by another.
root_idea.development: The lexical field distinguishes self-related shame from externally inflicted humiliation: خَزِيَ describes entering a disgraced or shamed state, خِزْيٌ names disgrace or ignominy, and أَخْزَى causatively makes another undergo that state.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form خَزِيَ.
Displayed under the normalized Form IV perfect citation form أَخْزَى.
Kept distinct from the homographic Form IV verb because this Quranic occurrence is nominal and comparative in use.
Displayed as the normalized active-participle citation form مُخْزٍ.
Displayed as the Quranic abstract noun خِزْيٌ.

senses.definition: To become abased, disgraced, or ashamed.
senses.usage_conditions: Intransitive: the subject enters a state of abasement or shame, whether arising from the subject's own condition or imposed by others.

senses.definition: To abase, disgrace, or put someone to shame.
senses.usage_conditions: Transitive causative: it may describe subjecting someone to humiliation or making that person ashamed of a shortcoming; Quranic uses include appeals concerning guests, worldly disgrace, and final judgment.
Comparative adjective, describing a greater degree of disgrace or humiliating effect.

senses.definition: One who causes disgrace; causing another to be abased or put to shame.
senses.usage_conditions: Active participle of Form IV, used substantivally in the Quranic occurrence for the agent who will disgrace.
A state or result of humiliation, often presented in Quranic contexts as the punitive or publicly manifest consequence of wrongdoing; distinct from the causative act expressed by أَخْزَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fall into trial, affliction, or an evil circumstance that exposes one to disgrace; to become confounded through disgrace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical Arabic branch of the Form I verb, distinct from the Quranic state of disgrace when the emphasis is on the affliction or resulting confusion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To vie or contend with another in mutual abasement, and to surpass or overcome him in it.
To compel someone to admit evidence or proof, thereby abasing or disgracing him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized causative construction in which acknowledged proof becomes the means of humiliation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To aid someone in, or make him keep to, a cause of shame, abasement, or disgrace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Construction involving a مَخْزَاة, a thing or circumstance that causes shame or abasement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing or circumstance that is a cause of shame, abasement, or disgrace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A cause or occasion of humiliation, rather than the state of disgrace itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a fixed expression, to utter a formula of apparent abasement as praise or benediction for someone whose action or speech is excellent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression أَخْزَاهُ اللهُ may be used admiringly or to ward off the evil eye, not as an actual imprecation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Base, abased, abject, vile, despicable, or ignominious.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Adjectival description of a person or thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A habit, practice, action, crime, sin, or act of disobedience of which one is or should be ashamed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Names shameful conduct, not merely the emotional state produced by it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bad, evil, or foul habit, quality, practice, or action that causes shame or abasement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Derived adjectival or nominal form referring to conduct that brings disgrace.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A trial or affliction into which one is made to fall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical Arabic use distinct from خَزْيَةٌ as a shameful act.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Affected by shame, especially intense shame over a bad or foul deed; also abased or despicable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Adjective with masculine, feminine, and plural forms; the shame may be emotional or associated with abasement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rendered base, abject, vile, or despicable by evidence proved against him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Passive-resultative description in which established evidence is the cause of abasement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an idiom for speech or poetry, excellent or approved to such a degree that its quality elicits praise for its speaker.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic Classical use, especially of كلامٌ مُخْزٍ or قصيدةٌ مُخْزِيَةٌ; it is not the ordinary Quranic agentive sense.

cautions: The Form I Quran occurrence نَخْزَىٰ is an imperfect inflected form and is displayed under the normalized citation form خَزِيَ.
أَخْزَىٰ is represented twice because the packet contains a Form IV verb group and a separate nominal comparative group; these homographic forms are kept distinct.

The Quran-focused discussion allows some uses of the Form IV verb to be understood through either self-related shame or externally imposed disgrace; the broad sense 'to put someone to shame' preserves that overlap without forcing an unsupported distinction.
No Maqayis entry was supplied; the root-level orientation and development therefore rely on the matched Quran-focused lexical discussion.
